subject: Planned retirement of TransitLayer v2 and subprocessor migration plan
messages:
From: TransitLayer Support <support@transitlayer.io>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: TransitLayer v2 decommission — partner notice and next steps

Hi Lauren,

As part of our platform consolidation, TransitLayer will retire the v2 processing stack on 2027-03-15. This affects transit.edge-proc (our telemetry relay) and the auxiliary ingestion tier that your services currently route to. We are notifying customers and downstream partners now to give time for contract amendments and subprocessor re-mapping.

What we are sharing today: 
- A short decommission summary (attached PDF) that lists affected endpoints and timing.
- A suggested migration map for partner subprocessors.

Impact for Redwood: based on our records, the traffic for your account is routed through TL-edge-3 (Hong Kong ingress) -> TL-core-us (San Jose) -> third-party observability: EdgeSight. We propose moving Redwood’s telemetry export to our new unified relay (TransitLayer v3) and updating the subprocessor roster to include our new transit-relay provider (RelaySphere).

Action requested from Redwood by 2027-01-20: 
1) Confirm whether Redwood accepts RelaySphere as a replacement subprocessor for telemetry.
2) Provide a point of contact for a short security checklist exchange (SOC2 artifacts, TLS cipher list, endpoint IP ranges).
3) Sign the contract amendment we will route via DocuSign (we will send a draft).

Attachment: transitlayer-v2-decommission-summary.pdf

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Success | TransitLayer

---
Note: If you need an extended timeline for regulated customers, reply and we can discuss options for a phased cutover.

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: TransitLayer v2 decommission — partner notice and next steps

Forwarding TransitLayer’s notice. Quick thoughts and asks:

- We need a short technical assessment of RelaySphere. Jonas, can your team validate TLS, IP ranges, and whether they store any persistent logs that could be considered personal data?
- Marissa / Legal: TransitLayer will push a contract amendment; we should check DPA language and any new processor additions. If RelaySphere is a subcontractor, we need the same indemnity/data transfer guards.
- Kimberly / ProdSec: confirm whether our telemetry routing config can switch without an app change (we try to handle via routing policies). If not, we’ll need an ops window.

I attached a quick spreadsheet (redwood-subprocessor-mapping-20270109.xlsx) mapping our flows to TransitLayer’s proposed mapping — fill in columns: Accept? Evidence link? Cutover window.

Tentative internal timeline: 
- 2027-01-20: Redwood decision on RelaySphere inclusion
- 2027-02-01: Exchange security evidence; legal signoff on contract amendment
- 2027-03-10 to 03-15: Planned cutover window (TransitLayer target 03-15)

Please reply with status updates in-thread. If anyone needs more time for evidence collection, flag now.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-mapping-20270109.xlsx

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@transitlayer.io>, support@transitlayer.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TransitLayer v2 decommission — partner notice and next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks for the heads up and the decommission summary. We’ve reviewed the high level and propose the following: 

1) Redwood is provisionally OK with RelaySphere being added to TransitLayer’s subprocessor roster for telemetry export only, pending security evidence (SOC2 type II or equivalent, endpoint IP ranges, and confirmation of no long-term PII retention).
2) Proposed technical cutover approach: staggered rollout by tenant region (US first), optional roll-back path to TL-core-us. We will use feature-level routing policies to test on 5% of traffic for 48 hours before increasing.
3) Contract amendment: please send the DocuSign envelope. We need an amendment that: 
   - Adds RelaySphere to the subprocessor list with clear scoping (telemetry export only),
   - Preserves existing data export and encryption language,
   - Adds requirement for 30 days’ notice for future subprocessor swaps.

Attachments we’re sending with acceptance: redwood-subprocessor-mapping-20270109.xlsx (filled for US region) and a draft contract amendment (contract-amendment-draft.docx). Please confirm receipt and share the security checklist contact.

Best,
Lauren

> On Fri, Jan 9, 2027 at 9:12 AM TransitLayer Support <support@transitlayer.io> wrote:
> > (original notice attached)

Attachment(s): redwood-subprocessor-mapping-20270109.xlsx, contract-amendment-draft.docx

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aisha@transitlayer.io, support@transitlayer.io
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TransitLayer v2 decommission — partner notice and next steps

Aisha / TransitLayer team — 

We reviewed the draft amendment Lauren attached. Legal has two redlines we need included before we can sign: 

1) Subprocessor obligations: RelaySphere must be contractually bound to the same data protection obligations as TransitLayer; please add a flow-down clause and provide a copy of RelaySphere’s processor agreement or a written attestation.
2) Cross-border transfer clarity: if RelaySphere routes telemetry through non-US jurisdictions for processing or forwarding, we need confirmation of safeguards (e.g., SCCs or equivalent) and the list of countries involved.

Technical team, please upload the filled mapping spreadsheet to the linked drive folder and drop a short runbook for the 5% canary test. Jonas, flag if RelaySphere requires any TLS profile changes.

Provided TransitLayer accepts those modifications and provides the requested evidence, Legal can sign by 2027-01-25. Also, please include a DocuSign envelope ID in-thread when you send the amendment so we can track it in our procurement system.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: contract-amendment-draft.docx (redlines requested)
